To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed an online tool that predicts hair colour from a small number of SNPs and identified 12 SNPs that have a strong effect on hair colour in Europeans.
we identified 12 most strongly hair colour-associated SNPs in six genes and developed a compact SNP marker set for the prediction of hair colours in Europeans with informative probabilities.
we developed and validated a compact set of 12 SNPs for hair colour prediction, and that we implemented the predictive approach in an online tool.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of a predictive approach to hair colour assignment from a set of informative SNPs.
developing a compact SNP marker panel and predictive model for hair colour prediction in European populations.

the development of an SNP based method for the prediction of hair colour from a small number of SNPs, which can be used to provide probative information on hair colour of unknown donors in forensic cases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HIrisPLEX assay is the best available method to predict hair colour in European population.

a set of 10 SNPs (rs12821256, rs12913832, rs1805008, rs11574437, rs16891982, rs1426654, rs11548643, rs28777, rs28780 and rs1805007) can be used to provide a hair colour assignment with an informative probability of 0.8 in 90% of the population and 0.9 in 80%.

the HIrisPLex assay is the best choice for forensic purposes and for the purpose of hair colour prediction, but that the 12 SNPs presented in this study are a good choice if the HIrisPLeX assay cannot be applied for some reason.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a small number of SNPs can be used to predict the hair colour of a DNA donor with high probability, which can be used in forensic casework to narrow down the suspect list.
a compact set of 12 SNPs can predict hair colour with high informative probabilities in a majority of cases.
the combination of a few SNPs is able to predict hair colour with high accuracy and can be applied for forensic casework.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a compact set of 6-8 SNPs can provide reliable hair colour inference in most European populations.

hair colour prediction from SNP profiles in Europeans can be accomplished with high accuracy using a small number of SNPs and that a probabilistic approach is a viable alternative to direct assignment.
the prediction of hair colour from a small number of informative SNPs in a compact assay is a promising approach for forensic and anthropological studies, and can be applied to other populations.
